sources.entry: stanza - The Stanford NLP Group's official Python library, supporting 60+ languages.

summary.one_liner: Stanza is the Stanford NLP Group's official Python NLP library, offering neural pipelines for many human languages plus a wrapper for the Java Stanford CoreNLP software.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a neural NLP pipeline in Python covering 60+ languages, with models for Universal Dependencies treebanks (v2.8) and NER models for a few widely spoken languages. The pipeline produces sentence and word annotations such as dependency parses, with a Document/Sentence object model. It includes an official Python wrapper for accessing Java Stanford CoreNLP, configured via the CORENLP_HOME environment variable. The README also mentions biomedical and clinical English model packages for syntactic analysis and NER on biomedical literature and clinical notes. All neural modules (tokenizer, MWT expander, POS/morphological tagger, lemmatizer, dependency parser, NER) can be trained on your own CoNLL-U or BIOES data by running training from the source repository.
use_cases: Part-of-speech tagging and lemmatization in many languages
Tokenizing and sentence splitting multilingual text
Parsing biomedical literature or clinical notes
Calling Java Stanford CoreNLP from Python
how_to_run: doc = nlp("Barack Obama was born in Hawaii.")
notable: Neural pipeline supporting 60+ languages from one Python library
Official wrapper for Java Stanford CoreNLP accessible from Python
Biomedical and clinical English model packages
Trainable modules using CoNLL-U and BIOES formatted data
Batching guidance: concatenate documents separated by blank lines for speed
caveats: Installing via Anaconda does not work for Python 3.10; use pip there
Using the CoreNLP wrapper requires separately downloading Stanford CoreNLP and model jars
Training custom models requires cloning the git repository; the Pipeline interface does not support training
Requires PyTorch 1.3.0 or above as a dependency
